A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LADM research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-training experiments, Proof-Pile perplexity, retrieval and LongBench evaluations, ablations, and appendix results on training budgets and short-context tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and adds ProLong results under larger training budgets.

M1.justification: Equation 4 changes the stated AFS distance weight from raw span distance to distance divided by N. This is a limited scoring-rule revision; with N fixed at 256, it uniformly rescales scores without changing rankings. The calculator, aggregation pipeline, training objective, and implemented stride settings remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pile training coverage, Proof-Pile evaluation, Needle-in-the-Haystack task, LongBench tasks, and short-context benchmarks. The additional ProLong training budgets introduce no new dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The training-budget comparison expands from Random and LADM in v1 Table 3 to include ProLong at 1B and 2B tokens in v2 Table 4. ProLong already participated in the main evaluations, but its inclusion in this particular comparison is new.

E3.justification: v2 adds 2B-token ProLong training conditions for all four evaluated models. Other stated model configurations and training settings remain stable. The Proof-Pile sample count and selection procedure become unspecified, so an actual change to that evaluation sample cannot be established.

E4.justification: Section 6.1 extends the training-budget analysis to test whether 1B-token LADM retains an advantage against 2B-token ProLong. The weight ablations, stride analysis, appendix calculator-budget study, and qualitative data examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report three experiments with different random-sampling seeds and averaged LongBench performance for Random. No uncertainty intervals or significance tests are added. The new parentheses in Table 10 show score differences from original models, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises all perplexities, while retaining LADM's leading ranking; for example, Llama2-7B LADM at 32K changes from 2.372 to 2.453, without establishing identical evaluation samples. v2 Table 4 adds 2B-token ProLong results. Main LongBench and underlying appendix scores remain unchanged. A new inconsistency appears: Table 4 reports 64.62 for Llama2-13B ProLong's 1B-token code score, versus 64.42 in Table 3.

T1.justification: Section 6.2 adds explicit computational-complexity expressions for PFS, AFS, and CDS, replacing a qualitative discussion of stride costs. Equation 4 also introduces distance normalization by N. Removing stride indexing from the displayed equations is explicitly described as a clarity simplification, not removal of sampling.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same attention-based dependency-selection contribution, reported 2.16% average LongBench improvement, and claim of outperforming random sampling with half the training tokens.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting contextual coherence to data quality, ProLong's isolated-segment limitations, and ablation outcomes are retained. The stated limitations remain selector overhead, no experiments above 13B parameters, and restriction to 32K contexts.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer in the abstract footnote. However, Section 4.4 and Table 2 remove v1's disclosure of 100 randomly selected Proof-Pile samples without supplying a replacement count or selection rule. Appendix B's training implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds background citations on long-chain reasoning, video/image processing, and long-form generation, plus discussion of Zhu et al. (2024)'s collinear attention approach. This broadens related-work coverage while preserving LADM's central positioning against ProLong.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar corrections and rewrites parts of the scoring and efficiency explanations. It also updates affiliations and adds acknowledgments. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded training-budget table moves from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 4, while the main LongBench table becomes Table 3. Table 10 adds colored parenthetical differences beside existing averages. Other floats shift position, but all nine figures retain their graphical content and the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Adding the 2B-token ProLong comparison addresses a specific gap in v1's training-efficiency evidence, which tested additional training only for Random. The code pointer and explicit complexity discussion also aid scrutiny. These gains are limited by unexplained perplexity revisions accompanied by loss of the evaluation sample count, and the new 64.62/64.42 inconsistency. The stronger efficiency comparison nevertheless provides a modest overall improvement.
